name: absorb blocks by XOR into part of a wide state between permutations, then squeeze output from the same part
mechanism: keep a state much wider than the output; XOR each message block into the exposed part of the state and apply a fixed permutation to the whole; when the message is consumed, read the exposed part as output, permuting again for more; the hidden part of the state is never directly touched by input or read as output

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'SHA-3 (SHA3-224, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, SHAKE128, SHAKE256)' in section Computer science / Cryptography:

fails_when: security is bounded by the hidden capacity, not the output length
instances: SHA-3 (SHA3-224, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, SHAKE128, SHAKE256)
